open_points.subject: context: source file and delivered photo model boundary
open_points.text: The deliverer does not offer such a copy. The file stays in the folder
open_points.question: Are a file in the Syncthing folder and the photo created in the Portal two different models with different identities, or lifecycle states of one Photo model?
options: Separate SourceFile and PortalPhoto models
One Photo entity spans the folder and Portal
Only PortalPhoto is a runtime model; folder entries are unmodelled input values
open_points.default_guess: Use separate SourceFile and PortalPhoto entities because the file can remain in the folder without any Portal photo being created.

witness.initial: A conflict copy exists in a project’s Syncthing folder and has never been delivered.
events: The deliverer scans the folder and rejects the conflict copy.
The deliverer offers it and the Portal stores the delivered photo hidden.
outcomes: One source-file entity survives the scan and later causes creation of a distinct Portal-photo entity.
One Photo entity changes from an unoffered folder state to a hidden delivered Portal state.
witness.observer: The deliverer, Portal persistence layer, and owner inspecting identifiers or history

open_points.subject: context: Syncthing conflict copy representation
open_points.text: Syncthing keeps the other version as a conflict copy beside it.
open_points.question: What model fact distinguishes a conflict copy from an ordinary photo before it is offered?
options: A status or eligibility field on the ordinary source-photo model
A distinct ConflictCopy model or discriminated variant
No runtime model is created for a conflict copy
open_points.default_guess: Represent it as a source-file entity with an explicit conflict status so its lifecycle through a later rename is expressible.

witness.initial: A folder contains an ordinary photo and its Syncthing conflict copy.
outcomes: The deliverer reads two source-photo entities and sees that one has conflict status.
The deliverer creates a model only for the ordinary photo and treats the conflict copy as pre-model input.
witness.observer: The deliverer and any audit or inspection surface listing discovered files

open_points.subject: context: source photo identity
open_points.text: The file stays in the folder, and the owner who wants that version renames it
open_points.question: What makes the source photo the same entity across observations: its path or filename, filesystem identity, content, or a minted identifier?
options: Path or filename identity
Filesystem object identity
Content-derived identity
A service-minted opaque identity
open_points.default_guess: Use a service-minted opaque entity identity and store the current path as mutable data.

witness.initial: A conflict copy exists at a conflict-copy pathname.
events: The owner renames it without changing its bytes.
outcomes: The second observation is the same source-photo entity with a changed path.
The second observation is a newly identified source photo because the path changed.
witness.observer: The deliverer, deduplication logic, and owner viewing processing history

open_points.subject: context: source photo minting
open_points.text: after which it is an ordinary photo.
open_points.question: Who mints the identity of the ordinary source photo after the rename, and from what evidence?
options: The deliverer mints it when scanning the renamed folder entry
The filesystem or Syncthing identity is adopted
The owner’s rename action creates or supplies the identity
The identity is derived from the file content or path
open_points.default_guess: Have the deliverer mint an opaque source-photo identifier on first eligible observation, from the observed folder entry while retaining path and content fingerprints as facts.

open_points.subject: context: conflict-copy rename lifecycle
open_points.text: the owner who wants that version renames it, after which it is an ordinary photo.
open_points.question: Does renaming change the status of the existing source-photo entity, or terminate the conflict-copy identity and create a new ordinary-photo identity?
options: The same entity transitions from conflict_copy to ordinary
The conflict-copy entity ends and a new ordinary-photo entity is minted
No entity exists until the rename, when an ordinary-photo entity is first minted
open_points.default_guess: Keep one source-file entity and transition its classification from conflict_copy to ordinary.

witness.initial: The deliverer has already observed and recorded a conflict copy.
events: The owner renames that exact file.
outcomes: The recorded entity changes status and retains its history.
The recorded conflict entity remains historical and a new ordinary-photo entity appears.
witness.observer: The owner viewing history and any component preventing duplicate processing

open_points.subject: context: conflict-copy provenance
open_points.text: Syncthing keeps the other version as a conflict copy beside it.
open_points.question: Must the model record which ordinary file or version a conflict copy conflicts with, and is that provenance retained after the owner renames it?
options: Record a durable conflict-of relationship and retain it after rename
Record conflict provenance only while conflict status applies
Record only conflict status, with no relationship to another file
Do not model conflict provenance or status
open_points.default_guess: Record conflict status and a conflict-of reference while it is a conflict copy, then retain the provenance as immutable history after rename.

witness.initial: Two conflict copies with identical visible content sit beside different ordinary photos.
events: The owner renames both conflict copies into ordinary filenames.
outcomes: Each renamed photo retains which original/version produced it.
Both are ordinary photos with no model fact linking them to their former conflicts.
witness.observer: The owner or an auditor investigating why a version was delivered

open_points.subject: context: offer action model access
open_points.text: The deliverer does not offer such a copy.
open_points.question: Which model does the offer action read to decide that nothing is created in the Portal, and does it record any lifecycle status for the rejected conflict copy?
options: Offer reads a SourceFile status and records it as excluded
Offer accepts only an OrdinaryPhoto variant, so conflict copies never reach the action
Folder discovery suppresses conflict copies before any runtime model or offer action exists
open_points.default_guess: Have offer read an explicit SourceFile classification and record an excluded-conflict status without creating a PortalPhoto.

witness.initial: A conflict copy is present and visible to folder discovery.
events: The deliverer performs its delivery flow.
outcomes: A modeled source entity is read and marked excluded while no Portal photo is created.
The entry is filtered before model creation, leaving no modeled record that it was considered.
witness.observer: The owner checking why a folder file was not offered and the operator inspecting delivery history

open_points.subject: context: renamed copy versus prior Portal photo identity
open_points.text: after which it is an ordinary photo.
open_points.question: If the same bytes or Syncthing version were already delivered to the Portal from another filename, does the renamed conflict copy identify the same deliverable photo or a new one?
options: Content/version identity makes it the same deliverable and it is not created again
Source-file identity makes it a distinct deliverable and a new hidden Portal photo is created
The source entity is distinct but points to the existing Portal photo
open_points.default_guess: Treat the renamed source file as distinct but link it to an existing Portal photo when their durable content identity matches.

witness.initial: An ordinary file has already produced a hidden Portal photo; a conflict copy with the same bytes remains beside it.
events: The owner renames the conflict copy.
The next delivery flow reads the renamed file.
outcomes: No new Portal photo is created because the deliverable identity is content-based.
A second hidden Portal photo is created because the renamed source file has a distinct identity.
witness.observer: The owner reviewing hidden photos and the client if the owner later shows both
